title: "Ranking Model"
description: "A model that orders candidate items by estimated relevance, preference, or utility."
term: "Ranking Model"

difficulty: "Intermediate"

## Simple explanation

A ranking model decides which items should appear first in a list. A search
engine, for example, estimates which results are most useful for a query and
orders them accordingly.

## Technical explanation

Ranking methods include pointwise models that score items individually,
pairwise methods that learn preferences between pairs, and listwise methods
that optimize properties of an ordered list. Features may describe the
query, item, user, or their interactions; evaluation often uses metrics such
as NDCG or mean reciprocal rank.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Ranking is central to search, recommendation, feed ordering, and retrieval
pipelines. The order affects exposure and user outcomes, so offline metrics,
latency, freshness, diversity, and responsible treatment of candidates all
matter.

## How it works

The system generates candidate items, computes features, and applies a
scoring or preference model. It sorts candidates by score, optionally
applying constraints or reranking stages. Training labels can represent
clicks, judgments, or preferences and should be interpreted with their
collection biases in mind.

## Practical example

A document-search service can retrieve a broad set using lexical and vector
search, then apply a ranking model to order passages for the user's query.
Evaluate on held-out queries with relevance judgments and monitor the
production experience.

## Common misconceptions

- A high ranking score is not necessarily a calibrated probability.
- Click-derived labels reflect presentation and user behavior as well as
  relevance; they are not unbiased ground truth.
